questions.q: Describe two main functions of the Chief Minister.
questions.answer: (1) advises the Governor on the appointment of Council of Ministers and allocation of portfolios to them; presides over the meetings of the State Council of Ministers and also coordinates the functioning of different ministers; (2) The Chief Minister is required to communicate to the Governor all the decisions of the Council of Ministers. is the sole link of communication between the Council of Ministers and the Governor. questions.q: Describe any two powers of the Prime Minister related to the Council of Ministers.
questions.answer: (1) No money bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha without his/her prior recommendation. But in practice, it is the Prime Minister who makes and unmakes the Council of Ministers. It is on his/ her recommendations that the President appoints the members of the Council of Ministers and distributes portfolios among them. (2) He/She presides over the meetings of the Cabinet and communicates its decisions to the President. If, due to any reason, he/she submits his/her resignation, the entire Council of Ministers stands dissolved.

questions.q: Why do GDP and per capita income not effectively measure the quality of people's life?
questions.answer: (1) Its major indicator, the GDP is a specific measure of economic welfare that does not take into account important aspects such as leisure time, environmental quality, freedom, social justice, or gender equality. (2) Per capita income is only an average and does not show inequality of income, so it cannot tell whether the benefits of development reach the poor and disadvantaged.

questions.q: How does the new notion of security differ from the traditional notion? Give two points.
questions.answer: (1) In this background the new notion of peace and security is based on threats beyond military attacks. The new notion of peace and security also includes freedom of individuals from hunger, freedom from wants, diseases and epidemics, environmental degradation, exploitation and sub-human treatment. (2) In fact, peace and security is to be seen as the precondition to socio-economic development and to the maintenance of human dignity. But the new notion is focused on human peace and security or global peace and security.

Mutual hatred and suspicion disturbed the atmosphere of peace. (b) System of Alliances divided Europe into two hostile camps – Triple Alliance and Triple Entente – leading to tension and conflicts.

questions.q: What are the causes of the Naxalite movement? How can it be solved?
questions.answer: Causes: The youth who are engaged in violent activities of the movement belong to the sections of society, mostly the scheduled tribes, scheduled castes and dalits, that have been bearing the brunt of social discrimination and economic deprivation since ages. Solutions: Efforts are being made to accelerate the pace of development in those areas and to bring the youth in to the mainstream. The government should formulate a national policy about naxalite movement to prevent them effectively from disturbing peace and security, accelerate development activities in those areas, so that there is no discontent among youth and to motivate the naxalites to shun violence and join the mainstream.

questions.q: How did the Policy of Appeasement and the rise of Fascism lead to the Second World War?
questions.answer: (1) Germany was humiliated by the Treaty of Versailles and wanted revenge; Italy was angry at getting no colonies. (2) The German version of Fascism is known as Nazism. He promised to reverse post-war settlements and restore German power and glory. Both the Fascist and Nazi Parties glorified war and promised to their people that they would bring back the lost glory of their countries through war. (3) Germany annexed Rhineland in 1936, Austria in 1938 and Czechoslovakia in 1938, while Italy attacked Ethiopia. (4) This resulted in rivalry between Russia and Austria. Later, the whole of Czechoslovakia was annexed. (5) But Ethiopia was taken over by Italy in 1935. (6) Being capitalist countries, they wanted to check the spread of Communism. This Appeasement Policy reached its climax when Hitler invited the Prime Ministers of Britain and France to Munich in August 1938. The Munich Pact was signed by them in 1938, allowing Germany to annex Sudetenland in the Northern part of Czechoslovakia. (7) Later on Italy, Germany and other countries also joined the race. She signed the Rome-Berlin-Tokyo Axis with the fascist powers. United Nations Organisation was formed for peace and harmony in the world at the end of the war. (8) The scene was set for World War II when Germany attacked Poland on 1September 1939. Britain declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939.

questions.q: Explain the powers and position of the Governor of a State.
questions.answer: (1) Executive powers: appoints the Chief Minister and ministers, the Advocate General and heads of State commissions. (2) Legislative powers: summons, prorogues and dissolves the legislature, addresses it, nominates members, and assents to or returns bills or reserves them for the President. (3) In fact, the budget i.e. ‘the Annual Financial Statement’ of the State is prepared and presented by the State Finance Minister before the State Legislature, on behalf Moreover, no money bill can be introduced in the State Legislature without the recommendations of the Governor. He/She also has control over the State Contingency Fund. (4) Discretionary powers: chooses the CM when no party has a majority, reserves bills for the President, and reports for President's Rule under Article 356. (5) But the Governor acts as a nominal head, and the real executive powers are exercised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister. Normally, the Governor exercises all his/her powers on the advice of the Council of Ministers. (6) Secondly, the Governor acts as a link between the Centre and the State. be correct to say that the Governor is just a constitutional or ceremonial head. He/ She can exercise his/her powers effectively under certain circumstances, especially when there is political instability in the State. Since he/she is a link between the Centre and the State, he/she becomes very effective, if the central government sends directions to the State government.
